positioning.target_user: Kubernetes platform engineers and security teams who manage Network Policies
positioning.job: visualize and test Kubernetes Network Policies from the CLI
positioning.gap: maintained free OSS alternatives lack a CLI that both visualizes policies and tests connectivity between pods; browser tools (artturik, calico-visualiser) are unmaintained; illuminatio is archived; kubectl-reach only tests connectivity from a live pod, not policy validation

items.title: Restore CLI visualize and test commands against test-policy.yaml
items.why: The candidate claims to be a CLI tool for visualizing and testing Network Policies; the repo includes a test policy and test directory but the README is truncated, so the round-trip must be verified.
items.acceptance: Running `knetvis` against `test-policy.yaml` produces a visualization output and test results without errors.
items.quote: A powerful CLI tool for visualizing and testing Kubernetes Network Policies.

items.title: Pin and update Python dependencies; ensure CI passes on Python 3.8+
items.why: The project declares Python 3.8+ support and provides requirements files; dependency drift can break the revive.
items.acceptance: CI workflow passes on Python 3.8, 3.9, 3.10, 3.11, 3.12 with pinned dependencies in requirements.txt and requirements-dev.txt.

items.title: Expand test coverage for visualize and test code paths
items.why: The repo has a tests/ directory and test-policy.yaml; coverage ensures the revive stays verifiable.
items.acceptance: pytest coverage >= 80% for src/ modules; new tests exercise cross-namespace policy visualization.
items.quote: Structured codebase with 6 non-boilerplate source paths (ci-check.sh, images/Real-demo.gif, setup.py). Solid working baseline.

items.title: Implement cross-namespace connection visualization
items.why: Differentiation identifies 'Show cross-namespace connections' as a capability not covered by any maintained free OSS alternative; must_beat alternatives (artturik, gerald1248) are unmaintained browser tools.
items.acceptance: Given a multi-namespace NetworkPolicy fixture, `knetvis visualize` renders namespace-scoped edges and labels them in the output.
items.quote: Missing capabilities: 'Visualize network policies', 'Test connectivity between pods', 'Validate network policy files', 'Show cross-namespace connections', 'Generate visualizations of network policies' (5 not covered by any maintained free OSS alternative).

items.title: Add network policy file validation (lint) command
items.why: Differentiation lists 'Validate network policy files' as a missing capability in maintained alternatives; the candidate can own this gap.
items.acceptance: New `knetvis validate` command exits non-zero and reports errors for invalid NetworkPolicy YAML (missing required fields, bad selectors).
items.quote: Missing capabilities: 'Visualize network policies', 'Test connectivity between pods', 'Validate network policy files', 'Show cross-namespace connections', 'Generate visualizations of network policies' (5 not covered by any maintained free OSS alternative).

items.title: Add pod-to-pod connectivity test simulation (offline)
items.why: Differentiation lists 'Test connectivity between pods' as uncovered; kubectl-reach only tests from a live pod via ephemeral container, not offline policy simulation.
items.acceptance: New `knetvis test` command takes a policy set and pod labels, outputs allowed/denied matrix without a running cluster.
items.quote: tests network connectivity from an existing Pod to a target (IP, DNS, or Service) by injecting an ephemeral debug container

must_beat.how_to_win: Provide a maintained CLI that visualizes policies and tests connectivity offline, whereas the alternative is an unmaintained browser tool (last update 2024-11-28).
Deliver a CLI-first, zero-dependency visualization that works for vanilla Kubernetes NetworkPolicies, not just Calico, and is actively maintained.
Offer active maintenance and a simpler CLI workflow (no cluster scan required for validation), while illuminatio is archived.
Provide a maintained CLI with cross-namespace visualization; the alternative is unmaintained since 2023 and only outputs JSON/YAML/dot.
Enable offline policy simulation and validation, not just live connectivity tests via ephemeral containers.

risks: No external demand signals (demand_evidence score 0) — adoption may stay low.
Zero moat (moat score 0) — any contributor can replicate the CLI approach.
Candidate README is truncated; actual feature set unknown — revive may uncover missing core functionality.
All must_beat alternatives are unmaintained or partial overlap; market may not perceive a strong need for another tool.

organised.detail: A test path is visible in the root, so gate 2's execution loop can verify the REVIVE stage.
